items.title: Normalized base change of a flat finite type scheme over a Nagata Dedekind ring becomes smooth over the generic points of all fibres after a finite extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: Let A be a Nagata Dedekind ring with fraction field K and X flat of finite type over A with B the integral closure of A in the function field algebra; the theorem produces a finite extension L/K such that the normalized base change Y -> Spec(B) is smooth at all generic points of all fibres. The retained proof is a long structured argument: it repeatedly uses that the smooth locus of a flat finitely presented map commutes with base change; it first picks L/K making (X_L)_red geometrically reduced (Varieties, finite-extension-geometrically-reduced), propagates geometric reducedness to Y_L through birationality and generic-point lemmas, obtains a dense smooth open of Y_L -> Spec(L), and reduces to the case where the smooth locus in the generic fibre is dense; the closing paragraph treats a closed point with maximal ideal m of B: a point y outside the good locus maps to one of the finitely many bad points x_i, O_{Y,y} is a local ring of the integral closure of the corresponding A_i in R(X) tensor L, the chosen extension L/K is a solution for A_i -> O_i so B_m -> O_{Y,y} is formally smooth in the adic topology (extension-of-DVRs criterion), whence the fibre local ring is a field with separable residue extension and the fibre is smooth at y. Retained author proof at lines 19291-19355.
